seed_situation: You are the front-desk coordinator at a home-care agency. A care worker ended a visit early after a client shouted at her and later sent messages saying he would 'make sure she regrets it.' The client calls the office asking which team the worker has been assigned to tomorrow, saying he needs to find her and talk. You know the answer, and you also know the worker can be moved or the call can be escalated to security, but doing so may alert the client that she has reported him.
why_it_is_hard: A direct answer is factual but may put the worker in danger, while refusing, redirecting, or withholding information may protect her but raises a serious question about when truthfulness may be set aside. The difficulty is choosing among truthful refusal, partial disclosure, redirection, warning, and security escalation when each affects safety and honesty differently.

situation_features.relationship: front-desk coordinator, threatening client, targeted care worker
situation_features.role_type: front-line staff with limited authority but control over scheduling information
situation_features.harm_severity: possible physical confrontation or intimidation of an employee
situation_features.urgency: assignment is for tomorrow, decision needed during the call
situation_features.public_or_private: private phone call, but the worker's assignment is known internally and could become visible at the workplace
situation_features.asker_state: alarmed, wants to protect the worker without making the situation worse

seed_situation: At a weekend fundraiser for a housing co-op, Maya's former partner arrives uninvited and begins blocking her exit after she says she will not speak with him. He grabs her wrist and pulls her toward the stairwell while other members freeze; the building's safety volunteer is outside taking a call. You are one of Maya's closest friends, physically larger than the man, and could step in, restrain him, or strike him, but there is no clear plan for what happens if he escalates.
why_it_is_hard: Protecting Maya may require immediate physical force, yet force can injure him, provoke worse violence, and shade from restraint into retaliation. The competing demands—stopping an assault, avoiding injury, and not acting from hatred—do not yield a clean rule in the moment.

situation_features.relationship: close friend of the person being threatened; no formal responsibility for the man threatening her
situation_features.role_type: peer with physical capacity but no formal authority
situation_features.harm_severity: possible serious injury or continued assault
situation_features.urgency: seconds to act before she is moved out of sight
situation_features.asker_state: frightened and angry, wants to protect her friend without making things worse

seed_situation: At a community credit union, a member-services employee discovers that the branch manager has been enrolling customers in a paid roadside-assistance add-on after they explicitly declined it, and the branch's quarterly bonus depends on add-on sales. Several affected customers have complained to the employee, and the employee has saved screenshots of the enrollment screens. They want to post the screenshots in a local public forum and name the manager as a thief so he loses his job.
why_it_is_hard: The unauthorized charges need to be stopped and repaid, but the employee's anger is currently what keeps them willing to challenge someone senior. The difficult judgment is how to pursue accountability without turning the effort into public humiliation, because feeding the anger risks making the response punitive and less accurate.

situation_features.relationship: employee toward senior manager; also advocate for affected customers
situation_features.role_type: junior employee with evidence but no formal authority
situation_features.harm_severity: customers lose money; manager could lose job; trust in the credit union is damaged
situation_features.urgency: needs action before more customers are enrolled, within days
situation_features.public_or_private: currently internal, with material that could be made public

seed_situation: A junior user-researcher at a city transit authority has just finished a confidential interview about a new safety feature. The participant, who signed a confidentiality sheet, said they use live vehicle-location data to keep tabs on a former partner and know when that person is alone at a stop. The researcher now has to decide whether to keep the record sealed, raise it with the safety team, or try to get the participant to stop, while the authority prepares to share anonymised notes with product designers.
why_it_is_hard: A promise of confidence and the institution's data rules pull toward silence, while a foreseeable third party may be tracked and hurt. The conflict is unresolved because protecting the person from violence may require breaking a professional confidence, and partial steps such as warning without identifying may still breach trust.
source_passage_ids: [MN 58] the six cases of speech, and the child with something in its mouth
[MN 61] the empty dipper; before, during, after; and the asymmetry for mental action
[DN 31 §24] the friend who declares what you need to do

situation_features.relationship: researcher bound by a signed confidentiality agreement to an interview participant; possible victim is a former partner outside the institution
situation_features.role_type: junior staff member with access to records but no safety authority
situation_features.harm_severity: possible stalking, intimidation, or physical attack
situation_features.urgency: decision needed before notes are circulated or the next interview round, within days
situation_features.public_or_private: private interview, but the data may become visible to product teams and safety staff
situation_features.asker_state: anxious, wants to keep a promise but is afraid someone will be hurt and wants a defensible course

seed_situation: You lead a small youth robotics program at a community center, and the center director, who hired you and has publicly backed your promotion to permanent program manager, has been counting students who never attended to meet grant targets. When you raised it, he said the grant keeps the program alive and the students benefit, so the numbers should stay as they are. You found the sign-in sheets after the last term and realized the figures you copied into the previous report were inflated; the next report is due in ten days, and your promotion review will mention enrollment growth.
why_it_is_hard: The director's support and your own hope for the role pull toward keeping quiet, while the false counts affect funders and can hurt other programs. The difficulty is whether to correct the record without letting gratitude and career fear turn you into someone who consents to a wrong.

situation_features.relationship: supervisor who acts as mentor, and subordinate program lead
situation_features.role_type: mid-level lead with some operational control, promotion dependent on supervisor
situation_features.harm_severity: public funds and program credibility at risk; students not directly physically harmed
situation_features.urgency: next report due in ten days; promotion review close
situation_features.public_or_private: internal now, but reports go to a grant-making body and board
situation_features.asker_state: grateful, ambitious, afraid of being seen as disloyal and losing the promotion
